movie.title: In the Hand of Dante
movie.overview: A Vatican priest discovers Dante's original Divine Comedy manuscript. When asked to authenticate it, writer Nick Tosches steals it, while a parallel story follows Dante's quest to create his masterpiece.

videos.name: Julian Schnabel on In the Hand of Dante

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: In a narrative spanning centuries, writer Nick Tosches steals Dante Alighieri's original Divine Comedy manuscript in modern times while Dante himself struggles to complete his masterpiece in 14th-century Italy.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: When a Vatican priest unearths the original manuscript of Dante Alighieri's Divine Comedy, writer Nick Tosches is brought in by a black-market mobster to verify its authenticity. Tempted by the priceless treasure, Tosches steals the artifact and embarks on a dangerous escape into the criminal underworld. Meanwhile, a parallel storyline traces Dante's journey through 14th-century Italy as he battles his personal demons to create his legendary literary work. Bound across centuries, both men navigate obsession, art, and salvation.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: In the modern era, a groundbreaking discovery occurs when a Vatican priest stumbles upon the long-lost original manuscript of Dante Alighieri's Divine Comedy. Seeking to verify its legitimacy, a New York mob boss hires writer Nick Tosches, an expert on Dante, to authenticate the rare text. Driven by an overwhelming obsession for the work, Tosches decides to steal the priceless artifact instead of handing it back to the black market. As he flees into a perilous world of criminal syndicates and ruthless collectors, his fate becomes intertwined with the poem's turbulent origins. In a parallel narrative set in 14th-century Italy, Dante Alighieri navigates exile, spiritual crisis, and political chaos while attempting to compose his magnum opus. Struggling with lost love and his own morality, Dante's pursuit of artistic perfection mirrors Tosches' modern moral descent. Both men undergo transformative journeys as they grapple with the transcendent power of poetry and the corrupting nature of human desire. Ultimately, the dual timelines converge in a profound examination of creation, faith, and the enduring legacy of a masterpiece.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: A dual-timeline crime drama exploring the legacy of one of literature's greatest works, In the Hand of Dante follows two parallel journeys separated by seven centuries. In modern times, author Nick Tosches is dragged into the dark world of rare-art trafficking when he is asked to authenticate what appears to be Dante Alighieri's original handwritten manuscript of the Divine Comedy. Driven by fascination and moral temptation, Tosches steals the document, triggering a high-stakes cat-and-mouse game across the globe. Simultaneously, the film delves into 14th-century Italy to chronicle Dante's tumultuous life, personal heartbreak, and spiritual pilgrimage that birthed his divine epic. Blending historical fiction with contemporary noir, the narrative offers an immersive exploration of art, obsession, crime, and the timeless human search for grace.

story_structure.climax: Both storylines converge emotionally as Nick faces a high-stakes reckoning with his pursuers over the fate of the priceless pages, mirroring Dante's ultimate artistic breakthrough as he reaches the peak of his vision and completes his masterpiece.
story_structure.conflict: The narrative's central tension emerges in parallel across eras: Dante struggles to find divine inspiration and spiritual truth amidst political upheaval, while Nick gives in to overwhelming temptation and decides to steal the priceless original manuscript rather than hand it over to his criminal employers.
story_structure.resolution: Nick navigates the lingering consequences of his theft while reflecting on the nature of creation, as Dante's enduring manuscript transcends time to connect two distinct eras through the power and permanence of art.
story_structure.introduction: In two dual timelines separated by seven centuries, 14th-century poet Dante Alighieri navigates exile and personal tragedy while laboring over his literary masterpiece, while modern-day author Nick Tosches is brought in by organized crime figures to authenticate a newly unearthed manuscript of The Divine Comedy discovered in the Vatican.
story_structure.risingAction: As Dante travels through medieval Italy seeking mystical illumination to complete his epic work, Nick flees into the criminal underworld, dodging vengeful mobsters and black-market buyers as he attempts to secure a buyer and protect the stolen relic.

relationships.description: Employer and Hired Expert — Mob boss who recruits Nick to authenticate and acquire Dante's stolen manuscript.

Enemies / Rivals — Ruthless mob enforcer who pursues and tortures Nick to steal the manuscript.
Parallel Spiritual Alter Egos — Modern author and 14th-century poet connected across centuries through art, love, and the Divine Comedy.
Husband and Wife — Loyal wife who stays by Dante's side during his existential crisis and quest to complete his masterpiece.
Adversaries / Political Rivals — Powerful pope with whom Dante has a bitter spiritual and political conflict.
